answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a costly, non-transferable bond before it can transact, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes prohibitively expensive. Like an opal that reveals its flaws under light, the bond makes fake accounts easy to audit: if an agent misbehaves, its stake is slashed, and the loss mirrors the damage it caused. A gale of cheap identities cannot overwhelm a market when every identity carries a real, forfeitable cost.
